bottom: David Crowley's money is labor and party money. His committee, Crowley for Wisconsin, raised $10,203,455.52 from July 1 to September 23, 2026, per the [September cover page](https://campaignfinance.wi.gov/report-download/0105751-CF-2--2026_September_Report--ORIGINAL--cover--2026-10-01-04-10-96.pdf). Of that, $6,054,458.19 came from 52,279 individual contributions and $4,138,600.01 came from 62 transfers. Those transfers include $2,730,000 from the Democratic Party of Wisconsin and a long run of union PACs at or near the $86,000 cap, per the [transfers schedule](https://campaignfinance.wi.gov/report-download/0105751-CF-2--2026_September_Report--ORIGINAL--Transfers_in_table--2026-10-01-04-10-96.pdf). He is outspent on ads $40 million to $26 million, per AdImpact data cited by AP.
Four interests combine money with a live decision:

**Building trades unions and data centers.** Laborers, IBEW, Pipe Trades, Operating Engineers, Carpenters and Plumbers fund Crowley, and IBEW says it supports data center development. Crowley flipped at the October 21 debate to say he would sign a Republican repeal of the roughly $2 billion data center sales tax exemption.
**Public sector and teachers unions.** WEAC PAC and AFSCME People PAC each gave $86,000. Crowley says he would keep both voucher programs, which teachers unions oppose.

Tom Tiffany is running the most concentrated campaign in recent Wisconsin history. His state committee, Tiffany for Wisconsin, reported $26,314,950.42 raised from July 1 to September 23, 2026, and $24,200,000 of it arrived in eleven transfers from the Republican Party of Wisconsin, per the [September transfers schedule](https://campaignfinance.wi.gov/report-download/0104212-CF-2--2026_September_Report--ORIGINAL--Transfers_in_table--2026-09-30-22-09-04.pdf). In the same period the party took $22,000,000 from Richard and Elizabeth Uihlein and $5,600,000 from Diane Hendricks, per the [party's own filing](https://campaignfinance.wi.gov/report-download/0300173-CF-2--2026_September_Report--ORIGINAL--full--2026-09-30-22-09-47.pdf). The filings show the money in and the money out on matching dates; they do not show a direct pass through, and this file does not store one.
Four interests combine large money with a live decision:

**The Uihleins and Hendricks.** They put $27.6 million into the state party in one quarter and are also the main funders of the Assembly and Senate Republican committees that would pass a Tiffany agenda. Their live decisions are the use of the $3 billion surplus, voucher income limits, and the Senate confirmation of a new PSC majority.
**The Uihlein super PAC.** Restoration of America PAC got $10 million from Richard Uihlein in August 2026. It has spent about $12.5 million to help Tiffany, mostly on ads against Crowley.

D.t: David Crowley leads by 7.3 in the forecast and wins 88% of simulations. The cushion is about 220,340 votes; a one point swing is about 15,030 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +0.8 and D +15.7. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +5.9. Your best recent poll is Marquette University at D +6.9; your worst is Marquette University at D +2.9. 5 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Milwaukee, a projected net 205,680 votes; Dane, a projected net 193,373 votes; La Crosse, a projected net 14,216 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Brown, R +4.7, 4.3% of the vote; Outagamie, R +4.0, 3.2% of the vote; Racine, D +0.9, 3.1% of the vote; Winnebago, D +1.3, 2.8% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, David Crowley runs furthest behind in Waukesha, Ozaukee, Washington. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 89% of voters, 51 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.45 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 76% of voters, 53 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.79 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 55 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.12 points.
The forecast's worst groups for David Crowley: Immigration voters 19 to 80, Incomes $125K and up 40 to 59, Small counties 44 to 55. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.8M cash against $12.0M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.1 points away from David Crowley. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Cash: $12.0M in the bank against $2.8M for David Crowley.

R.t: Tom Tiffany trails by 7.3 and wins 12% of simulations. Closing it takes about 110,170 voters switching sides, or 220,340 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +15.7 and R +0.8. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +5.9. Your best recent poll is Marquette University at D +2.9; your worst is Marquette University at D +6.9. 5 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Waukesha, a projected net 45,133 votes; Washington, a projected net 27,105 votes; Fond du Lac, a projected net 10,285 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Brown, R +4.7, 4.3% of the vote; Outagamie, R +4.0, 3.2% of the vote; Racine, D +0.9, 3.1% of the vote; Winnebago, D +1.3, 2.8% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Tom Tiffany runs furthest behind in Sauk, La Crosse, Chippewa. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 89% of voters, 48 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.45 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 76% of voters, 46 to 53, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.79 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 44 to 55, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.12 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Tom Tiffany: Black voters 15 to 84, Corruption voters 28 to 71, Health care and Social Security voters 30 to 69. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$12.0M cash against $2.8M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.1 points toward Tom Tiffany. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
